title: Lesson 1 · AI foundations
kit: Most of this room already uses AI at work, in more than one tool. Before we build anything, one question: what is it actually doing when it answers?
Know what it does and where it fails.
Explain what generative AI does well and where it can be wrong.
chrome: By the end of this block:

title: A very well-read new joiner.
kit: It has read more than any associate ever will, so its drafts are fast and fluent. It has never seen this client's file, so it fills gaps with what is usual.

title: What it really does.
kit: A model trained on very large amounts of text that writes by predicting the most likely next word, one word at a time. That is why it reads, summarizes, extracts and drafts well.
Like the new joiner's fluent first draft…
…each word is likely. Likely is not the same as checked.
It predicts. It does not look things up unless you give it the source.

title: It writes by guessing the next word.
kit: It writes by guessing the next word.
At each step, every possible next word gets a score. The model picks one, adds it, and predicts again.
It predicts likely words. It does not check if they are true.
The cut-off test for Abdali Foods shows the invoice was posted in
chrome: What word comes next? Click one.
Now it predicts again, using the whole sentence so far
so it is a cut-off point.
